title: Task 1: Create justfile with default, run, test, check recipes
description:
## Goal
Deliver a working justfile at the project root exposing `just run` (with arg forwarding), `just test`, `just check` (fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo check), and a default recipe listing commands.

## Implementation

1. Study existing setup
   - Cargo.toml - crate name hello-hash, clap CLI (subcommands in src/main.rs)
   - src/main.rs - entry point; confirm subcommand names for verification (e.g. hello)
   - just 1.58.0 confirmed installed

2. Write the justfile (verification-first: recipes mirror cargo commands already proven on this crate)
   - justfile (new file at repo root):
     - `default`: @just --list
     - `run *args`: cargo run -- {{args}}
     - `test`: cargo test
     - `check`: cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo check
     - Comments above each recipe (shown by just --list)

3. Verification checklist
   - [ ] justfile - parses (`just --summary` or bare `just` lists recipes)
   - [ ] `just test` exits 0
   - [ ] `just check` exits 0 on clean tree
   - [ ] `just run <subcommand>` runs app with args forwarded
   - [ ] Negative check: intentionally misformat a file -> `just check` exits non-zero -> revert

## Success Criteria
- [ ] All 5 epic requirements demonstrably working via commands above
- [ ] Tests passing
- [ ] No extra recipes, no shell config, no swallowed failures (epic anti-patterns)
design:
## Goal
Deliver a working justfile at the project root (C:/Users/comrade77/Projects/rust_hello_hash/justfile) exposing `just run` (with arg forwarding), `just test`, `just check` (fmt + clippy -D warnings + cargo check), and a default recipe listing commands.

## Effort Estimate
~0.5 hours (single small file + verification runs)

## Implementation

1. Study existing setup (already done during refinement)
   - Cargo.toml - crate hello-hash, edition 2024
   - src/main.rs:14-29 - clap subcommands: `sign`, `generate-key`, `delete-key`
   - rust-toolchain.toml:4 - components = ["clippy", "rustfmt"] already pinned, so cargo fmt/clippy are guaranteed available
   - just 1.58.0 confirmed installed

2. Write the justfile
   - justfile (new file at repo root), exactly these recipes with comments (comments show in just --list):
     - `default`: @just --list
     - `run *args`: cargo run -- {{args}}
     - `test`: cargo test
     - `check`: cargo fmt --check && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings && cargo check

3. Verification checklist (run each, confirm expected result)
   - [ ] `just` (bare) exits 0 and lists run/test/check recipes
   - [ ] `just test` exits 0 (14 existing unit tests in src/main.rs pass)
   - [ ] `just check` exits 0 on clean tree
   - [ ] `just run sign --help` exits 0 and prints sign subcommand help (proves arg forwarding reaches clap)
   - [ ] Negative check: break formatting in src/main.rs (e.g. add trailing spaces), `just check` exits NON-zero at fmt step, then revert with git checkout -- src/main.rs

## Success Criteria
- [ ] Bare `just` lists all recipes (default recipe works)
- [ ] `just run sign --help` exits 0 printing clap-generated help (arg forwarding verified without triggering Windows Hello)
- [ ] `just test` exits 0, all tests pass
- [ ] `just check` exits 0 on clean tree
- [ ] `just check` exits non-zero when formatting is broken (failure propagation verified, not swallowed)

## Key Considerations (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

**Edge Case: sign/generate-key/delete-key are INTERACTIVE**
- `just run sign` triggers a real Windows Hello biometric prompt (src/main.rs:102-104, hello::sign uses KeyCredentialManager)
- Verification MUST use `just run sign --help` (clap prints help, exits 0, no Windows Hello call) NOT a real sign invocation

**Edge Case: run with no args**
- `just run` passes empty args -> clap errors 'subcommand required', app exits 64 (src/main.rs:202-204 confirms this behavior is tested)
- This is correct app behavior, not a justfile bug

**Edge Case: arg forwarding of flags**
- just may consume leading dashes itself; if `just run --help` misbehaves, use `just run sign --help` (flag after positional) as the canonical verification

**Prerequisite guaranteed by toolchain**
- rust-toolchain.toml pins clippy + rustfmt components; no separate component install step needed
- If run on a machine without just installed, recipes fail at command-not-found; acceptable (justfile is dev tooling)

**Anti-patterns (from epic, restated)**
- ❌ NO extra recipes beyond default/run/test/check (YAGNI)
- ❌ NO `|| true` or failure swallowing in check recipe
- ❌ NO Windows-specific shell settings (set windows-shell etc.) - all recipes are plain cargo invocations

title: Feature: hello-hash — Windows Hello Signature to SHA-256 CLI
description:
# Epic: hello-hash — Windows Hello Signature → SHA-256 CLI (Rust)

Source of truth: `SPEC.md` in the repo root (approved design). This epic is the immutable
contract; tasks adapt as we learn. Two decisions resolved during brainstorming:

- **Toolchain:** keep `edition = "2024"` / `rust-version = "1.95"` (existing Cargo.toml;
  installed toolchain). SPEC §8's "edition 2021 / MSRV 1.85" line is superseded — SPEC
  behavior remains normative.
- **Task tracking:** beads via `br` CLI in this workspace (bd/tm unavailable).

## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)

- **R1 — Sign & hash:** `sign` requests a signature of the challenge string via Windows Hello
  (`KeyCredential::RequestSignAsync`), computes SHA-256 over the returned signature bytes,
  and writes the digest to stdout.
- **R2 — Hash input:** SHA-256 is computed over the signature `IBuffer` bytes only. The
  challenge string itself is never hashed.
- **R3 — Challenge encoding:** challenge string converted to UTF-16LE via
  `CryptographicBuffer::ConvertStringToBinary(value, BinaryStringEncoding::Utf16LE)`,
  identical to the C++ service (`biometric_cipher_service.cpp:90`).
- **R4 — Key names match mfa_locker:** default key tag `mfa_demo_bio_key`; overridable via
  `--tag`.
- **R5 — Default challenge matches mfa_locker:** default challenge
  `locker_authentication_request`; overridable via positional argument.
- **R6 — Key management:** `generate-key` creates with
  `KeyCredentialCreationOption::FailIfExists`; `delete-key` removes via
  `KeyCredentialManager::DeleteAsync`.
- **R7 — No auto-create:** `sign` never creates a missing key; `OpenAsync` → `NotFound`
  exits with code 3.
- **R8 — Deterministic output:** same tag + challenge → same SHA-256 digest (TPM PKCS#1 v1.5
  deterministic signing). Nothing may break this (no randomization of challenge encoding).
- **R9 — Output discipline:** stdout receives only the 64-char lowercase hex digest +
  trailing newline; all diagnostics/errors to stderr.

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)

- [ ] `cargo build --release` succeeds with zero warnings.
- [ ] `hello-hash generate-key` creates the `mfa_demo_bio_key` credential (Hello prompt).
- [ ] `hello-hash sign "locker_authentication_request"` prints 64-char lowercase hex digest
      after successful Windows Hello prompt.
- [ ] `sign` twice with identical tag + challenge yields identical digests (R8).
- [ ] Signing same challenge with a different tag (fresh key) yields different digest.
- [ ] `hello-hash delete-key` deletes the credential; subsequent `sign` exits 3.
- [ ] Canceling the Hello prompt exits 2 with clear stderr message.
- [ ] stdout contains nothing but the digest on success.
- [ ] `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check` pass.
- [ ] Manual checklist (SPEC §10) executed by human — Windows Hello prompts cannot be
      automated; agent handles build/lint/unit tests, human runs the biometric checklist.

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO AES-GCM / encryption of any payload (scope: sign → hash → output only).
- ❌ NO hashing the challenge string instead of the signature bytes (correctness: R2 —
      plugin hashes `signatureResult.Result()`, not the input).
- ❌ NO auto-creation of key inside `sign` (compatibility: R7 — silent creation masks
      missing-key errors).
- ❌ NO default key tag other than `mfa_demo_bio_key` (compatibility: R4 — must interop
      with mfa_locker vault).
- ❌ NO `IAsyncOperation::get()` (correctness: removed in windows 0.62; blocking call is
      `.join()`).
- ❌ NO `match` on `KeyCredentialStatus` (correctness: newtype struct with associated
      constants in windows-rs — compare with `==`).
- ❌ NO async runtime (tokio etc.) — blocking `.join()` from `main` is MTA-safe
      (simplicity: KISS).
- ❌ NO extra output on stdout (usability: R9 — breaks piping/scripts).
- ❌ NO TODO stubs for the core sign flow (completeness: core flow must be implemented).

## Approach

Standalone Rust CLI using `windows` 0.62.2 WinRT projections
(`KeyCredentialManager`, `CryptographicBuffer`) with `sha2` 0.11.0 and `clap` 4 derive.
All WinRT calls live in `src/hello.rs` behind a small facade
(check_availability / open_credential / create_credential / delete_credential / sign).
Blocking on async via `.join()` from `fn main()` — no async runtime. A single `CliError`
enum carrying exit codes maps WinRT statuses/hresults to (exit_code, message) pairs per
SPEC §6–§7. Exit codes: 0 ok, 2 canceled, 3 not found, 4 already exists, 5 unsupported,
6 device locked, 7 prefers password, 8 unknown/internal, 64 usage.

## Architecture

```
hello-hash/
├── Cargo.toml        # clap 4.5 derive, sha2 0.11, windows 0.62.2 (4 features)
└── src/
    ├── main.rs       # CLI parsing (clap), exit-code dispatch, top-level CliError
    ├── hello.rs      # all WinRT: availability check, open, create, delete, sign
    └── hash.rs       # sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String (pure, unit-testable)
```

Reference implementation (C++, source of truth) at `../mfa_locker/packages/biometric_cipher/windows/`:
sign flow `windows_hello_repository_impl.cpp:48-75`; SHA-256 over signature
`winrt_encrypt_repository_impl.cpp:20-34`; create `:77-99`; delete `:101-121`;
status mapping `:143-170`; availability `:19-46,133-141`.

## Design Rationale

### Problem

`mfa_locker` derives its biometric AES key on Windows as
`SHA-256(RequestSignAsync(challenge))` inside a C++ WinRT plugin. A standalone Rust
equivalent is needed for experimentation, verification, and tooling outside the Flutter app.

### Research Findings

**Codebase (mfa_locker, verified present at ../mfa_locker):**
- `windows_hello_repository_impl.cpp:48-75` — sign flow: availability → OpenAsync →
  RequestSignAsync → status mapping.
- `winrt_encrypt_repository_impl.cpp:20-34` — SHA-256 over the signature buffer, then
  used as AES-256-GCM key.
- `example/lib/core/constants/app_constants.dart:23` — production key tag `mfa_demo_bio_key`.
- `lib/security/models/biometric_config.dart:41` — default challenge
  `locker_authentication_request` (example app never overrides `windowsAuthData`).

**External (windows-rs 0.62.2, verified 2026 per SPEC §8):**
- Feature flags: `Security_Credentials`, `Security_Credentials_UI`,
  `Security_Cryptography`, `Storage_Streams` (gates RequestSignAsync/Result()).
- Async blocking is `join()` (windows-future 0.3.2); `get()` removed in 0.62.
- `OpenAsync` does not create credentials; creation is `RequestCreateAsync`.
- `KeyCredentialStatus` is a newtype struct with constants (Success=0 …
  SecurityDeviceLocked=6); not matchable as an enum.

### Approaches Considered

1. **Standalone Rust CLI, windows-rs + sha2** ✓
   - Pros: exact WinRT API parity with the C++ plugin; minimal deps; hash logic pure-Rust
     and unit-testable; `.join()` keeps the program tiny.
   - Cons: Windows-only; relies on windows-rs projection quality.
   - **Chosen because:** user explicitly requested Rust standalone; behavioral parity with
     the plugin.

2. **Rust with Win32 NCrypt/TPM directly**
   - Pros: lower-level control.
   - Cons: raw NCrypt does not reproduce Hello consent-on-sign semantics; plugin itself
     uses KeyCredentialManager for signing. **Rejected:** behavioral divergence.

3. **C++ port of the plugin sources**
   - Pros: trivially faithful.
   - Cons: user explicitly requested Rust and a separate project. **Rejected.**

### Scope Boundaries

**In scope:**
- `sign` / `generate-key` / `delete-key` subcommands with `--tag` option.
- Exit-code mapping and stderr diagnostics per SPEC §6–§7.
- Unit tests for hash + argument parsing; manual checklist support.

**Out of scope (deferred/never):**
- AES-256-GCM encryption/decryption (consumer's concern).
- Cross-platform support (Windows only).
- Config file / persistent storage.
- Base64 or other digest encodings (hex only).
- Public key attestation, TPM status reporting, isKeyValid checks.

### Open Questions

- Exact clap exit-code configuration for usage errors (64 vs clap defaults) — cosmetic.
- Whether `DeleteAsync` on a non-existent tag errors or succeeds silently across Windows
  versions — treat incoming `windows::core::Error` as exit 8; refine after manual testing.
- Confirm on target machine that `sign` output is stable across reboots (R8 across TPM
  sessions — expected, key is persistent).

Both tasks closed. Commits 615c512..6ea0f48..(spec fix) on master.

title: Task 1: Pure-Rust core — hash module + CLI argument parsing (TDD)
description:
# Task 1: Pure-Rust core — hash module + CLI argument parsing (TDD)

**Effort estimate:** 4–6 hours.

## Goal

Deliver the automatable half of `hello-hash`: `src/hash.rs` with `sha256_hex()` and the
clap-derive CLI surface in `src/main.rs` (subcommands `sign`/`generate-key`/`delete-key`,
correct defaults, `CliError` exit-code dispatch). No WinRT calls yet (that is Task 2,
which will be created after learning from this one). Everything in this task is
unit-testable without Windows Hello.

## Implementation

1. Study reference material
   - `SPEC.md` §5 (CLI spec), §6 (exit codes), §9 (module layout) — normative.
   - `Cargo.toml` — deps already declared (clap 4.5 derive, sha2 0.11, windows 0.62.2).
     Edition 2024 / rust-version 1.95 (decision from brainstorming).

2. Write tests first (TDD)
   - `src/hash.rs` inline `#[cfg(test)]` known-answer tests (constants below were
     precomputed with Python `hashlib`, independent of the code under test — do NOT
     re-derive them from `Sha256::digest` in the test):
     - `test_sha256_empty_input` — SHA-256 of empty input =
       `e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855`
     - `test_sha256_abc` — SHA-256 of `"abc"` =
       `ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad`
     - `test_sha256_boundary_55_bytes` — 55 × 'a' (final padding block boundary) =
       `9f4390f8d30c2dd92ec9f095b65e2b9ae9b0a925a5258e241c9f1e910f734318`
     - `test_sha256_boundary_56_bytes` — 56 × 'a' (requires extra padding block) =
       `b35439a4ac6f0948b6d6f9e3c6af0f5f590ce20f1bde7090ef7970686ec6738a`
     - `test_sha256_boundary_64_bytes` — 64 × 'a' (full block) =
       `ffe054fe7ae0cb6dc65c3af9b61d5209f439851db43d0ba5997337df154668eb`
     - `test_output_is_64_lowercase_hex_chars` — output length == 64 and every char in
       `[0-9a-f]` (catches uppercase/padded hex bugs; use input `b"X"` and assert
       against the char set)
   - CLI parsing tests (`src/main.rs` `#[cfg(test)]`, using `Cli::try_parse_from`):
     - `test_default_tag_and_challenge` — `["sign"]` yields tag
       `mfa_demo_bio_key`, challenge `locker_authentication_request` (catches
       wrong/default-missing bugs; R4/R5)
     - `test_explicit_challenge_overrides_default` — `["sign", "my challenge"]`
     - `test_explicit_tag_overrides_default` — `["sign", "--tag", "other"]`
     - `test_empty_string_challenge_is_used_not_default` — `["sign", ""]` yields
       challenge `""` NOT the default (catches clap default-fallback bug; an empty
       challenge is a legal value that will be UTF-16LE-encoded to an empty buffer)
     - `test_unicode_challenge_accepted` — `["sign", "привет 🔐"]` parses to the same
       string (catches encoding/lossy-conversion bugs at the CLI boundary; surrogate
       pairs included via the emoji)
     - `test_tag_with_spaces_accepted` — `["sign", "--tag", "my key tag"]`
     - `test_unknown_subcommand_errors` — `["frobnicate"]` fails to parse
     - `test_subcommand_required` — `[]` (no args) fails to parse (SPEC §5.1: no
       implicit default command)
     - `test_second_positional_rejected` — `["sign", "a", "b"]` fails to parse
     - `test_generate_key_and_delete_key_default_tag` — both parse with default tag
   - `CliError` mapping tests:
     - `test_cli_error_exit_codes` — each variant maps to its SPEC §6 code:
       UserCanceled→2, KeyNotFound→3, KeyAlreadyExists→4, HelloUnsupported→5,
       SecurityDeviceLocked→6, UserPrefersPassword→7, Unknown→8, Usage→64
     - `test_cli_error_message_prefixes` — stderr messages start with `Error: ` and
       match SPEC §6 wording (e.g. `user canceled the operation.`)

3. Implementation checklist
   - [ ] `src/hash.rs` — `pub fn sha256_hex(bytes: &[u8]) -> String` using
         `sha2::Sha256::digest` + lowercase hex encoding (iterate bytes with
         `format!("{:02x}")` or fold into a String; must not allocate per test's
         performance needs — simple approach fine)
   - [ ] `src/main.rs` — clap derive `Cli` struct: subcommand enum with `Sign {
         challenge: Option<String>, tag: String }` (challenge via
         `#[arg(default_value = "locker_authentication_request")]` on positional),
         `GenerateKey { tag: String }`, `DeleteKey { tag: String }`; every `tag` uses
         `#[arg(long, default_value = "mfa_demo_bio_key")]`. NOTE: if clap's
         `default_value` on an optional positional swallows `""`, use
         `Option<String>` + explicit fallback logic that distinguishes `Some("")`
         from `None` (test above enforces this).
   - [ ] `src/main.rs` — `CliError` enum (variants listed in tests above), with
         `fn exit_code(&self) -> i32` and `fn message(&self) -> String` per SPEC §6.
   - [ ] `src/main.rs` — `fn main()` builds args, on `Cli::try_parse` error prints
         usage to stderr and exits 64; dispatches subcommands; on `CliError` prints
         `Error: <message>.` to stderr and exits with `exit_code()`; on success of
         `sign` prints ONLY the digest to stdout.
   - [ ] Dispatch stubs: `sign`/`generate-key`/`delete-key` return
         `Err(CliError::Unknown("not implemented: WinRT layer (task 2)".into()))`
         (exit 8) — these are the ONLY permitted stubs, explicit and temporary,
         replaced in Task 2.
   - [ ] Unit tests as specified above, all in `#[cfg(test)]` modules.

4. Verification commands
   - `cargo test` — all unit tests pass
   - `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — zero warnings
   - `cargo fmt --check` — clean
   - `cargo build --release` — zero warnings

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 6 hash known-answer/property tests pass with the precomputed constants above
- [ ] All 10 CLI parsing tests pass (defaults R4/R5, overrides, empty-string challenge,
      Unicode, unknown subcommand, no implicit default command, extra positional rejected)
- [ ] All `CliError` exit-code and message tests pass per SPEC §6
- [ ] `cargo test` green; `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean;
      `cargo fmt --check` clean; `cargo build --release` zero warnings
- [ ] No WinRT calls added in this task (hello.rs deferred to Task 2)

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO `unwrap()`/`expect()` in production code paths (tests may use them)
      (robustness: panics turn mapped errors into exit code 101 / stack traces,
      violating R9's clean-stderr contract).
- ❌ NO TODO comments without an issue ID (traceability).
- ❌ NO `unimplemented!()`/`todo!()` macros — dispatch stubs must return
      `Err(CliError::Unknown(...))` so exit-code wiring is real and testable
      (completeness: the error path is the deliverable of this task).
- ❌ NO deriving test constants from `Sha256::digest` itself (tautology — tests must
      catch a broken hash implementation, not confirm it).
- ❌ NO printing anything to stdout except the digest (R9).

## Key Considerations (ADDED BY SRE REVIEW)

**Edge Case: empty-string challenge**
- `hello-hash sign ""` must sign an empty UTF-16LE buffer, NOT fall back to the
  default. Verify clap `default_value` semantics for positionals; if `""` triggers
  the default, restructure to `Option<String>` with explicit `Some("")` handling.
  This is the most likely silent bug in this task.

**Edge Case: Unicode challenge**
- Challenges are arbitrary user strings; HSTRING conversion (Task 2) handles
  UTF-16. At the CLI boundary assert lossless parsing of non-ASCII incl. non-BMP
  (surrogate pairs, e.g. 🔐 = U+1F510).

**Edge Case: hex encoding correctness**
- Lowercase only, no `0x` prefix, no padding — R9. The property test plus
  known-answer tests jointly catch uppercase/padded/wrong-length output.

**Exit code 64 wiring**
- SPEC §5.4: usage errors exit 64, not clap's default 2. Implement via
  `Cli::try_parse` + manual `std::process::exit(64)` after printing the clap error
  to stderr (`err.use_stderr()` / print `err.render()`). Unit-testable by asserting
  parse failure; the exit itself is thin glue.

**Release build with zero warnings**
- Success criterion `cargo build --release` with zero warnings — do not add
  `#![deny(warnings)]` blindly; just keep the tree warning-free (SPEC allows deny).

**Scope discipline**
- Do not start `src/hello.rs` in this task. Task 2 (WinRT layer) is created by
  executing-plans AFTER this task's learnings, per iterative-task principle.

comments.author: unknown
comments.text: All substeps complete: 18 unit tests green (hash known-answer + CLI parsing + CliError mapping), clippy -D warnings clean, fmt --check clean, release build zero warnings. Verified exit codes: sign stub=8, usage error=64. Commit 3ae68f7. Learnings: (1) clap default_value keeps provided empty string; (2) #[expect(dead_code)] needs cfg_attr(not(test)) scoping since test targets use everything; (3) #[expect] annotations must be removed when task 2 wires the variants.

title: Task 2: WinRT layer — Windows Hello operations in hello.rs
description:
# Task 2: WinRT layer — Windows Hello operations in hello.rs

## Goal

Implement `src/hello.rs` (all WinRT calls: availability check, open, create, delete, sign)
and wire it into `main.rs` dispatch, replacing the Task 1 stubs and removing the
`#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))]` annotations. After this task the binary is
feature-complete; only the human manual checklist (SPEC §10) remains.

## Context

Completed `...k2t.1` (Task 1): CLI parsing, CliError mapping, hash module — 18 unit tests
green, all lint gates clean. Learnings: clap keeps provided empty strings over defaults;
`expect(dead_code)` must be `cfg_attr(not(test), ...)`-scoped; exit-code wiring (8, 64)
verified end-to-end.

## Implementation

1. Study references (source of truth, C++):
   - `../mfa_locker/packages/biometric_cipher/windows/windows_hello_repository_impl.cpp`
     lines 19–46 (availability), 48–75 (sign), 77–99 (create), 101–121 (delete),
     133–170 (status mapping).
   - `../mfa_locker/.../winrt_encrypt_repository_impl.cpp` lines 20–34 (hash over
     signature), `biometric_cipher_service.cpp` lines 85–92 (UTF-16LE conversion).
   - SPEC §5 (behavior), §7 (status table), §8 implementation notes (join(), == on
     status, HSTRING, MTA threading).

2. `src/hello.rs` facade (private helpers + pub functions used by main):
   - `fn map_status(status: KeyCredentialStatus) -> Result<(), CliError>` — pure,
     unit-testable. Success(0)→Ok, NotFound(2)→KeyNotFound, UserCanceled(3)→UserCanceled,
     UserPrefersPassword(4)→UserPrefersPassword, CredentialAlreadyExists(5)→
     KeyAlreadyExists, SecurityDeviceLocked(6)→SecurityDeviceLocked, anything else
     (incl. UnknownError=1)→Unknown with status code in message. Compare with `==`
     against associated constants — NEVER `match` (newtype struct).
   - `fn to_utf16le(value: &str) -> windows::core::Result<IBuffer>` —
     `CryptographicBuffer::ConvertStringToBinary(&HSTRING::from(value),
     BinaryStringEncoding::Utf16LE)`. Unit-testable without Hello prompt.
   - `fn check_availability() -> Result<(), CliError>` —
     `KeyCredentialManager::IsSupportedAsync()?.join()?`; if false →
     `UserConsentVerifier::CheckAvailabilityAsync()?.join()?` mapped to a reason string:
     `DeviceNotPresent`→"device not present",
     `NotConfiguredForUser`→"not configured for user",
     `DisabledByPolicy`→"disabled by policy",
     `DeviceBusy`→"device busy",
     `Available`→is still Ok (Hello available even though KeyCredential unsupported),
     any other value→"unknown error occurred"
     → `Err(HelloUnsupported(reason))` (except the Available case). Testable without
     prompt.
   - NOTE (from C++ reference `windows_hello_repository_impl.cpp:133-141`): a distinct
     `Error: Windows Hello is not supported.` (bare, no reason) occurs only when the
     biometry status is neither "supported" nor any of the four mapped availability
     values — reachable in Rust only if `CheckAvailabilityAsync` throws a WinRT error;
     that path is covered by the `?` → Unknown conversion. The bare message is therefore
     not separately implemented.
   - `fn open_credential(tag: &str) -> Result<KeyCredential, CliError>` —
     `OpenAsync(&HSTRING::from(tag))?.join()?`; map_status on
     `retrieval.Status()?`; then `retrieval.Credential()?`.
   - `fn create_credential(tag: &str) -> Result<(), CliError>` —
     `RequestCreateAsync(&HSTRING::from(tag), KeyCredentialCreationOption::FailIfExists)?
     .join()?`; map_status on `result.Status()?`.
   - `fn delete_credential(tag: &str) -> Result<(), CliError>` —
     `DeleteAsync(&HSTRING::from(tag))?.join()?` → Ok(()) on success; WinRT error →
     `Err(Unknown(err message))` → exit 8 (epic decision; SPEC §5.3 says exit 7 —
     discrepancy documented in Open Questions, refine after manual testing).
   - `fn sign(tag: &str, challenge: &str) -> Result<Vec<u8>, CliError>` —
     check_availability → open_credential → to_utf16le →
     `credential.RequestSignAsync(&buffer)?.join()?` → map_status on
     `result.Status()?` →
     `let mut bytes = Array::<u8>::new();
      CryptographicBuffer::CopyToByteArray(&result.Result()?, &mut bytes)?;`
     → return `bytes.to_vec()` as signature bytes.
     If `Status` is Success but `Result()` throws/is null, the `?` propagates a WinRT
     error → Unknown → exit 8. A zero-length signature yields a 64-char digest of empty
     bytes (legal output; spec has no minimum-signature-length requirement).

3. Wire `main.rs` `run()`:
   - `Sign { challenge, tag }` → `hello::sign(&tag, &challenge)?` → print
     `hash::sha256_hex(&bytes)` + newline to stdout (ONLY this on stdout), Ok.
   - `GenerateKey { tag }` → check_availability → create_credential → confirmation to
     stderr, Ok.
   - `DeleteKey { tag }` → check_availability → delete_credential → confirmation to
     stderr, Ok.
   - Remove both `cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code))` annotations.

4. Threading: call `.join()` directly from the synchronous call chain (main thread MTA,
   no async runtime, no COM STA init) per SPEC §8.

5. Unit tests (all prompt-free):
   - `map_status`: 8 cases — all seven known constants + one unmapped value (e.g. 99)
     → Unknown.
   - `to_utf16le`: `"abc"` → bytes `[0x61,0x00,0x62,0x00,0x63,0x00]`; `""` → empty
     buffer (catches wrong-endian/double-conversion bugs).
   - `check_availability`: completes and returns (Ok or Err(HelloUnsupported) — both
     valid outcomes on this machine), does not panic. On success this also validates
     that the `Storage_Streams`/`Security_Credentials` feature flags in Cargo.toml are
     correct for the chosen windows-rs version.

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All map_status unit tests pass (8 cases incl. unmapped status)
- [ ] to_utf16le tests pass (correct little-endian byte layout, empty string)
- [ ] check_availability test passes without panic
- [ ] All Task 1 tests still pass (18) — no regressions
- [ ] Dispatch stubs replaced by real WinRT calls; `expect(dead_code)` annotations removed
- [ ] `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo fmt --check`,
      `cargo build --release` all clean
- [ ] Manual checklist (SPEC §10) handed to user for human verification
- [ ] `hello-hash sign` stdout is exactly 65 bytes (64-char hex + `\n`) — verify with
      `hello-hash sign | wc -c` during manual run

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)

- ❌ NO `WH_CBT`/`SetWindowsHookEx`/`AllowSetForegroundWindow` workarounds (the C++
      hooks exist only because the Flutter host steals focus; a console CLI owns the
      foreground — SPEC §8 explicit non-replication note).
- ❌ NO `IAsyncOperation::get()` — `.join()` only (removed in windows 0.62).
- ❌ NO `match` on `KeyCredentialStatus` — `==` with associated constants only.
- ❌ NO async runtime / tokio — blocking join() from main.
- ❌ NO auto-create of key inside sign (R7) — NotFound → exit 3.
- ❌ NO unwrap()/expect() on WinRT Results in production paths — every `join()?`,
      `Status()?`, `Credential()?`, `Result()?` handled via CliError.
- ❌ NO stdout output except the digest (R9) — confirmations to stderr.
- ❌ NO hashing of the challenge string (R2) — hash the signature bytes only.

## Open Questions

- SPEC §5.3 says delete-key WinRT errors exit 7, but §6 table maps 7 to
  UserPrefersPassword and "any other hresult" to 8. Epic resolved this as exit 8;
  confirm during manual testing and update SPEC if needed.
- Whether `DeleteAsync` on a non-existent tag errors or succeeds silently (manual test).
- Whether this dev machine has Windows Hello enrolled — if not, availability tests still
  pass; prompt flows are deferred to the human checklist anyway.

title: Feature: justfile with run, test, check commands
description:
## Requirements (IMMUTABLE)
- Requirement 1: A justfile exists at project root (C:/Users/comrade77/Projects/rust_hello_hash/justfile)
- Requirement 2: `just run [args...]` builds and runs the app, forwarding extra args to the clap CLI (`cargo run -- {{args}}`)
- Requirement 3: `just test` runs the full test suite (`cargo test`)
- Requirement 4: `just check` runs cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets with -D warnings, and cargo check; fails if any step fails
- Requirement 5: Bare `just` (default recipe) lists available recipes

## Success Criteria (MUST ALL BE TRUE)
- [ ] `just run hello` (or equivalent subcommand) executes the app and forwards args
- [ ] `just test` exits 0 with all tests passing
- [ ] `just check` exits 0 on clean tree and exits non-zero if fmt/clippy fail
- [ ] `just` with no args lists recipes
- [ ] All tests passing
- [ ] Pre-commit hooks passing (if configured)

## Anti-Patterns (FORBIDDEN)
- ❌ NO extra recipes beyond run/test/check/default (YAGNI: user explicitly asked for only these three commands)
- ❌ NO Windows-specific shell configuration (portability: all recipes are plain cargo invocations, already platform-agnostic)
- ❌ NO swallowing failures (correctness: check must exit non-zero when fmt/clippy/check fail; no `|| true`)

## Approach
Create a single minimal justfile at the project root with four recipes: default (just --list), run (arg forwarding via *args), test (cargo test), check (fmt --check && clippy -D warnings && cargo check). No shell config needed since all recipes invoke cargo directly.

## Architecture
- justfile - sole new file at repo root; wraps cargo commands for the hello-hash binary crate

## Design Rationale
### Problem
Developer must remember and type full cargo command sequences (fmt --check, clippy flags). A justfile provides short, memorable, consistent commands.

### Research Findings
**Codebase:**
- Cargo.toml - binary crate hello-hash, edition 2024, rust-version 1.95, clap-based CLI
- src/main.rs, src/hash.rs, src/hello.rs - 3-file crate, no existing justfile
- just 1.58.0 installed and available in PATH

**External:**
- just docs - variadic args via `run *args` recipe parameter; default recipe runs on bare `just`

### Approaches Considered
1. **Minimal justfile with run/test/check/default** ✓
   - Pros: Exactly matches request, zero bloat, already cross-platform
   - Cons: build/clean added later only if needed
   - **Chosen because:** YAGNI - user asked for exactly run, test, check

2. **Full-featured justfile (build, release, clean, fmt-fix, etc.)**
   - Pros: Covers future needs
   - Cons: Unrequested recipes violate YAGNI
   - **Rejected because:** Scope creep beyond explicit request

3. **Windows-specific justfile (set windows-shell, pwsh scripts)**
   - Pros: Explicit shell guarantees
   - Cons: Unneeded complexity for pure cargo invocations
   - **Rejected because:** All recipes are platform-agnostic cargo commands

### Scope Boundaries
**In scope:**
- justfile with default, run, test, check recipes
- Arg forwarding in run recipe

**Out of scope (deferred/never):**
- build/release/clean/fmt-fix recipes - deferred until requested
- CI integration - not requested
- Cross-platform shell configuration - unneeded for cargo-only recipes

### Open Questions
- None blocking; clippy strictness level fixed at -D warnings per design
